author: nonretail_writer
central_thesis: Going into a US holiday Monday, Washington says Putin has decided to invade while Macron works toward a Putin–Biden summit, and the Fed is set to tighten into the hottest inflation in 40 years (2Y +46 bps over 20 observations, bear flattening to +45 bps). Portfolios should be built to survive a geopolitical gap rather than to chase carry: favour pricing-power staples, energy, defence, gold and Russia-supply-risk commodities (aluminium, grains, US gas) over long-duration growth, Russia-sensitive European financials and Polish assets. In China, stay long onshore easing (ASHR) against offshore platform regulation (KWEB).
sources_policy: Every cited [[nNNNN]] comes from feeds/2022-02-21.json.gz, was published before 2022-02-21T00:00:00Z and was re-checked against its exact headline wording, outlet, timestamp and window (news/previews 7 days, results 14, macro 35). Every number is either from cards/2022-02-21.json, quoted exactly with its session tag (US instruments 2022-02-18 close because of the Presidents' Day closure; crypto at the 2022-02-20 completed daily close; Treasury curve at the 2022-02-18 close), or from a headline cited in the same part. No numeric spot-FX is used: currency direction comes only from dated reporting (n0214 yuan, n1579 złoty, n0087 dollar), and DXY is quoted as an index. Previews (Truth Social release n0932, Maserati Grecale n0506) are presented only as pending events. No ID is used more than twice. No other date's feed, card, spec or draft was read. A generic scratch digest that another agent overwrote mid-session was discarded, and every topic was re-run directly for this date.
known_ambiguities_omitted: n1427 (CNBC) and n1440 (CNN): Biden agreeing 'in principle' to meet Putin. The White House statement may have come late Sunday US time, after 00:00 UTC, so it is omitted. Only the Guardian's Macron summit-idea framing (n1430) is used.
n1319 (CNN 'Photos: Russia invades Ukraine', stamped 2022-02-14): misdated rolling page describing events after the cutoff, so it is excluded.
Truth Social items n0932, n1766, n1763, n1742 and n1765: only n0932 is cited, as a preview of a pending App Store release. The launch outcome falls after the cutoff and is not stated.
Putin's recognition of the breakaway regions (evening of 21 February): unknown at the cutoff. It is treated only as a pending risk, via the separatists' recognition demand (n1412).

China loan prime rate (21 February, 01:15 UTC) and Japan flash PMI (21 February, 00:30 UTC): both after the cutoff. The text refers only to 'the next loan prime rate fixing' and 'the next official PMI', without dates or outcomes.
Separatist evacuations (19 February): there is no own-date headline, so they are not stated.

n0077 (ABC, 'ASX up, AGL rejects Atlassian billionaire's takeover bid', stamped 2022-02-20): probably describes the Monday 21 February ASX session and bid rejection, which fall after the cutoff, and it contradicts the card's 18 February ASX close (-1.02%). Omitted.
n0834 (Yahoo, '4 Top Stock Trades for Tuesday'): the publication timing is ambiguous and could be after the cutoff. Omitted.
n1209 (Euronews, 'German manufacturing slumps in October', stamped 2022-02-11): misdated October data. Omitted.
n1694 (Bankier, 'Inflacja bliska zeru…'): ambiguous and contradicts January CPI of 9.2% (n1597). Omitted.
n0887 (The Ankler, Roku -26%): its magnitude contradicts Reuters' 20% fall (n0793), so only Reuters is used.
n1019 (WSJ, Evergrande CEO sold bonds, 2022-02-10): company news older than the 7-day window, even though it is filed as a result. Omitted.
Reuters LIVE MARKETS blog posts n1274, n1264, n1229 and n1218: live and rolling pages. Omitted.
Spot-FX headlines n1193 (EUR/USD) and n1187 (pound/euro): omitted, and no numeric FX is quoted anywhere.
Promotional or low-quality items n0928 (100-bagger), n0980 (altcoins to buy), n1003 (Saitama Inu), n0687 (real-asset stocks to buy) and n0256 (The Sun tabloid): omitted.
n0137: source metadata 'MS NOW' is a later outlet name. Omitted.
Previews n0123 (Deere earnings preview) and n1009 (SoftBank earnings preview): not used to support any outcome. Deere's result is cited from Reuters (n0852).
DraftKings -21.62% on 18 February: no own-date results headline, so no cause is attributed. Only general sports-betting margin context (n1119) is given.
n0064 (WSJ): the headline does not clearly attribute 'won't follow the Fed' to board member Harper, so the text attributes it to the RBA as an institution.
